title: Period and season calendar v1
description: The six frozen periods of D-088 and the season lifecycle that governs the seasonal one. docs/product/ACCOUNTING_AND_TIME_CONTRACT.md owns time semantics and docs/architecture/SERVER_API_DATA_AND_RANKING_CONTRACT.md owns the ranking consequences; this schema is the machine-readable calendar. Country periods are absent because country leaderboards remain post-launch under D-052.

timezone.description: Every boundary is evaluated in one timezone for every participant. A local-timezone boundary would give participants in different places different periods and make one leaderboard compare two different windows.

boundary.description: iso-week starts Monday per ISO 8601. season-declared means the boundary comes from the season record rather than from the calendar. unbounded is the lifetime period, which has no start and no end.

late_claim_admission.description: How long after a period ends a claim whose interval falls inside it may still be admitted, keyed to standard_claim_lateness_seconds in policy-defaults-v1.json. A claim later than this is accepted into the ledger and excluded from the period, never silently backdated.

season.description: The five timestamps after starts_at must be non-decreasing in the order given. packages/schemas/planning-schema.sql enforces the same order as check constraints, so a season whose dates do not order that way cannot be inserted.

freeze_at.description: After this instant no further claim enters the season, however late its interval. The gap between ends_at and freeze_at is what a delayed offline claim has to arrive in.

close_at.description: The final generation seals here and becomes the archived standing. A correction after close produces a superseding generation rather than an edit.

appeal_window_ends_at.description: An appeal decided inside this window can still supersede the archived standing, which is what keeps the reversed state of the appeal machine reachable after a season closes.
